sanskrit: yā dhānyāt saṃbhavanti kṣetrād uptād varpitāta | kṛtād abhiprahāyyā naśyatetaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Those [demon-women] who arise from grain, from a field that has been sown, from what has been threshed — the fierce ones that attack what has been done, let those sadānvāḥ perish from here.

sanskrit: yāḥ puruṣāḥ pāpagandhāḥ sadā rukṣā visṛkpadī | tā vajreṇa samarpayan nirajetaḥ śacīpate ||
english: Those [women-demons] who take human form, who always have an evil stench, ever rough, with scattered feet — drive them away with the thunderbolt, expel them, O lord of Śacī!

sanskrit: ut tiṣṭhata nir dravata na va ihāsti nyañcanam | indro vaḥ sarvāsāṃ sākaṃ garbhān āṇḍāni bhetsyati ||
english: Rise up! Run away! There is no shelter for you here. Indra will shatter together all your embryos and eggs at once.

sanskrit: indra jahi sthūlaśaṃkhāṃ mṛṇīhi durṇaśīṃ kuham | arāyīṃ śakadhūmyaṃ nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Indra, strike down the thick-shelled one; crush the ill-fated kuha; the greed-demon, the one reeking of dung-smoke — we destroy these sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: kim āsutāṃ nagnahvam ajamāyuṃ ca nighnatīm | viṭiṭiṅgāḥ pratodinīr nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Why do they brew the naked-caller and the goat-snatcher who slays? The sharp-prodding viṭiṭiṅga-demons — we destroy those sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: yasyāsutaṃ randhayadhve yūyaṃ bhaṇvāḥ sadānvāḥ | tṛṣṭaṃ kṛṇutāṇḍaraṃ yadā rasena tṛpyata- -āt surām ava mehatha ||
english: You bhaṇva-sadānvā demons subdue whose brew? Make the broth bitter! And when you are sated with the liquor — then you urinate out the surā.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ pītvāvamakty atho śīrṣakty ā śaye | tā ekānnadūṣaṇīr nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: After drinking of her [brew], one vomits and then lies down with a splitting head-pain. Those that corrupt the shared meal — we destroy those sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: apārogāñ chakadhūmān vṛkṣāṇāṃ yantu satvaram | atho durhārdaso gṛhaṃ pra mṛśantv arāyyaḥ ||
english: Let the foul-smelling dung-smoke demons go quickly to the trees! And let the evil-hearted arāyī-goblins stroke the house [to their ruin].

sanskrit: tāsām ekācchavakā śaṅkāvaṅkā vanekṛkur hasanaikā kanikradā | sarvāsāṃ bhaṇvā vaḥ sākaṃ nāmadheyāni vidmasi | yati jātāni vas tati naśyatetaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Among those [demons]: the solitary lurker, the bent-horned one, the forest-screamer, the sole laugher, the chattering one — all your names together, O bhaṇvā-demons, we know them. As many as have been born among you, let that many perish from here, O sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: sahasvatīṃ pra harāmi- imāṃ śālāṃ viṣāsahim | sadānvāghnīm oṣadhiṃ jaitrāyācchā vadāmasi ||
english: I drive forward the herb endowed with power, this victorious [plant] that overcomes poison, the herb that slays the sadānvāḥ — we speak it forth for victory.

sanskrit: duḥsaṃkāśe bhīmacakṣo nagne bhaṇve sadānve dhrājiṃ tviṣiṃ śucim agnim arāyi kim ihecchase | dhūmaṃ mābhi pra gāyi ni stauṣāmi sadānve ||
english: O ill-seen one, terrible-eyed, naked bhaṇvā, sadānvā — the rushing, blazing, pure fire [is here] — what do you want here, arāyī? Do not come near my smoke! I press you down, O sadānvā.

sanskrit: kaṅkyekā prakhidaikā kim ic chāntyabhiśrayā | caranti naktaṃ durṇāmno arāyīḥ sūtikaiṣyas tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: The solitary heron-like one, the solitary digger — what do they seek, lurking by the fire? The ill-named arāyī-demons that wander at night seeking women in childbed — we drive those away from here.

sanskrit: apakrathām abhiśrayām ānṛtyantīṃ kutūhalām | kusūlīṃ rathabhañjanīṃ khalāj jātās trikūkvas tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: The boaster, the fire-croucher, the dancing one full of restless curiosity, the granary-haunter, the chariot-breaker, the three-humped ones born from the threshing floor — we drive those away from here.

sanskrit: yā vikeśīr unmadityā- -urarā ghoracakṣavaḥ | śīrśāṇy anyā anyāsāṃ vitāvantīr ivāsate sadānvā brahmaṇaspate paro bhrūṇāny arpaya ||
english: Those disheveled, maddened, broad-chested, terrible-eyed ones — some sit as if stretching out the heads of others, O sadānvā-demons. O Bṛhaspati, hurl their embryos far away!

sanskrit: yāsāṃ gandho nānārūpaḥ paryaiti puruṣaṃ pathi | tā agniḥ sahatām ito jātavedāḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Those whose odor of many forms circles a person on the path — let Agni Jātavedas overpower and drive away those sadānvāḥ from here.

sanskrit: yāḥ puruṣaṃ dahyamānaṃ śūnyam agnau jighatsanti | bhaṇvā niṣkuṣṭā nāmāsi muṣṭāgreṇa sadānvās tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Those who wish to devour a person being cremated, [who prey upon] the vacant [body] on the fire — you are called bhaṇvā niṣkuṣṭā ('the winnowed one'); we drive those sadānvāḥ away from here with the tip of the fist.

sanskrit: yā ucitā āvapane śuṣkaṃ khādanti maṣmasaṃ vaḍavā gardabhīr iva | nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Those accustomed to the fire-pit who eat dry ash, like mares and she-asses — we destroy those sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: garbhān ekaḥ prati morśaṃ yā adanti sadānvāḥ | ucitās tanvaṃ striyā gāva ā rohiṇīr iva tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Those sadānvāḥ who devour fetuses one by one at every morśa, who are accustomed to the body of a woman like red cows [attached to their spot] — we drive those away from here.

sanskrit: yāḥ pitṛyāt saṃbhavanti- -indrajā naḥ sadānvāḥ | apa mityam ivābhṛtaṃ punas tā prati dadmasi ||
english: Those sadānvāḥ who arise from the ancestral realm, born of Indra, coming to us — we send those back again, as if returning a load that was brought.

sanskrit: āmādinīḥ krūrādinīr anagnigandhyādinīḥ | amuṃ paretyoddhitaṃ śavam atta sadānvāḥ | śavaḥ kevala ācāraḥ kim u śālāsv icchatha ||
english: Eaters of the raw, eaters of the cruel, eaters of what smells of no fire — eat that corpse carried off to the beyond, O sadānvāḥ! A bare corpse is your proper fare; what indeed do you seek in houses?

sanskrit: yāḥ kumārīr yāḥ sthavirā yuvatīr yāḥ sadānvāḥ | sarvā yantu kurūṭinīḥ kulīnādhenu sarpatv arāyīr abhibhā itaḥ ||
english: Those sadānvāḥ who are girls, who are old women, who are young women — let all go as kurūṭinī-demons, as the cowless outcast clan; let the arāyī-goblin creep away in awe from here.

sanskrit: tābhyo rudro visṛjat tviṣim adhvagaghātinīm | tā astā hantu vidyutā vajreṇānaparādhinā | tāsāṃ tvaṃ śakra moc chiṣa indra bhaṇvāḥ phalīkuru ||
english: Let Rudra loose against them his fury that slays wayfarers; let the archer smite them with lightning and the faultless thunderbolt. O Śakra, do not spare them; O Indra, shatter the bhaṇvā-demons!

sanskrit: kumārān ekā sthavīrān yā adanti prakhādinīḥ | tā indro hantu vṛtrahā yā devo viśvād rakṣāṃsi sedhati ||
english: Those gluttonous ones who devour boys — some — and old men — let Indra the Vṛtra-slayer destroy them, the god who repels all demons from all sides.

sanskrit: yāś ca dāsīr asurāṇāṃ manuṣyebhyaś ca yāḥ kṛtāḥ | ubhayīs tāḥ parā yantu parāvataṃ navatiṃ nāvyā ati ||
english: Those who are slave-women of the asuras and those made [to harm] humans as well — let both kinds go far away, beyond the distance of ninety [river-crossings] by boat.

sanskrit: yāsāṃ ghoṣaḥ saṃgatānāṃ vṛkāṇām iva gaṅgaṇaḥ | pracaṅkaśāmaivaharāṃ prayacchantīṃ pratigrahāṃ nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: Those whose din when gathered sounds like the growling of wolves — those that offer pracaṅkaśā ['the harsh snatcher'] as a gift-in-return — we destroy those sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: yāni sāyaṃ yathāsthāmād rātrīṃ yakṣāṇi prerate | agniṣ ṭā sarvā sāhantyo viśvād rakṣāṃsi sedhatu ||
english: The yakṣa-spirits that are stirred up at evening from wherever they station themselves to roam the night — let Agni, overpowering them all, repel those demons from all sides.

sanskrit: yā ṛkṣīkāḥ kalīlāndā- -apsu jātāḥ pulīkayāḥ | gopā āsām eko veda yato jātāḥ sadānvās tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Those ṛkṣīkā-demons, the egg-laying kalīlā-ones, the pulīkā-beings born in the waters — one guardian alone knows their origin. Those sadānvāḥ who have been born — we drive them away from here.

sanskrit: gurucchāyām ūrdhāryaṃ śiśumākāṃ pratiśrukām | atiduhnāṃ vicalantīṃ vitūlumām | sarvāś caṇḍasya naptyo nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: The heavy-shadowed one, the one borne upward, the child-devourer, the echo-maker, the over-milker, the wanderer, the cotton-tufted one — all these granddaughters of Caṇḍa among the sadānvāḥ we destroy.

sanskrit: āvadantīṃ nāmahūkāṃ taṃstanīkāṃ vṛṅktapadīm | udradantīm anāsikāṃ nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: The loudly speaking one, the name-caller, the thundering one, the claw-footed one, the protruding-toothed one, the noseless one — we destroy these sadānvāḥ.

sanskrit: vāvadākām albhaṣāsāṃ vijavrāṃ labruvaṃ lavum | arāyīṃ vācamejayāṃ nāśayāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: The incessant babbler, the unintelligible mutterer, the disheveled one, the blabbering one, the roaming one, the arāyī, the one that makes the voice tremble — we destroy these sadānvāḥ.
